- If sentiment is positive (≥ 0.2) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- If sentiment is negative (≤ -0.3) in recent days, model tends to underestimate prices; increase forecast slightly.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at 10–15% above peak or adjust downward after 3–5 days.
- Model exhibits strong mean reversion bias in early forecast horizon (e.g., 1–5 days ahead) — adjust for gradual decline if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- For 15+ day forecasts, model often fails to capture downward trend; apply downward bias if sentiment is negative or price has recently fallen.
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative spikes (e.g., -0.2 to -0.5), model tends to ignore them; add a 5–10% downward adjustment to forecast.
- If model forecast is rising steadily with no sentiment change, it often overestimates; cap forecast at 1–2% above recent 7-day average.
